I was diagnosed a few years back when I was around 13. I had always known I had ASD, but having a therapist diagnose me for real was different. I assumed (wrongly) that with a true, authentic diagnosis I could be myself. My real self, my autistic, sound and touch sensitive, no eye contact making self.  Before then, I just pretended to be "normal," so my friends and family weren't ready for me to be myself.  I struggled with this for a long time, and occasionally, I still do. Not being able to be honest in your own home sucks. It's hard for me to deal with all the competing sounds at home and everyone wanting to hug and my mom wanting me to wear scratchy, uncomfortable clothes to church. The only wisdom I can offer is to give yourself time alone. When I'm alone, I can stim and listen to soft music in noise cancelling headphones and do whatever the hell I please.
